method: land use change analysis of very high resolution orthophotos at three sites, direct observations
predictors: residential expansion, fishing districts, hotels and tourism, garbage dumps, industrialization and port development, energy installations, agriculture, livestock, aquaculture
finding: Mangroves at three Greater Libreville sites lost 35.6 to 46.9 ha each from 2007 to 2020, 0.8 per cent a year, mainly to residential, port and other urban expansion.
gap_quote: However, the annual rate of urban mangrove deforestation in Gabon's Estuary Province is higher than the mean rate of global mangrove deforestation.

data: ESA CCI land cover at 300 m, MODIS collection 6 burned area at 500 m
method: overlay of MODIS burned area with ESA CCI land cover change, assessment of 14 influencing factors, method not named
predictors: 14 fire-related, climatic, topographic, ecological and socioeconomic factors, burned area size, vegetation cover diversity, aspect, fire intensity, slope
finding: Post-fire land cover change covered 0.36 to 0.74 per cent of annual burned area, most common in Brazil, Argentina and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
gap_quote: Fire, as a strong disturbance type, can exert significant impacts on the biosphere, hydrosphere , geosphere, cryosphere , atmosphere and human society.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, 34 REDD+ projects
data: not stated
method: baseline allocation for assessed risk, a dynamic vector spatial predictor of deforestation with risk-based allocation of the national forest reference emission level
predictors: dynamic vector predictor, not described further
finding: BAAR mapped deforestation risk and allocated the national reference level to 34 REDD+ projects in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, directing finance to high risk areas.
gap_quote: While the REDD+ market is shifting from project-based to nested approaches as countries increase their efforts to meet nationally determined contributions (NDCs) to the Paris agreement's global climate target, methodologies for allocating national baselines are not yet formalized and tested, despite an urgent need to scale the market.

data: remotely sensed activity data, emission factors from the national forest inventory
method: forest reference emission level from activity data and emission factors, adjusted with a land use model of the agriculture sector, Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis
validation: projections compared with the 2000 to 2015 observed trend
finding: Adjusted for population, economic and urban growth, southern Cameroon's projected emissions for 2020 to 2030 averaged 47 per cent above 2000 to 2015, with the adjustment driving uncertainty.
gap_quote: Many countries, however, find it difficult to establish a credible adjusted reference level.

place: Cameroon, Djoum, Mintom, Ngoyla and Yokadouma forest massif
data: land-use transition data, source not stated
method: accounting of emissions and removals from land-use transitions, net REDD+ balance
finding: Emissions rose from 2005, peaked in 2012, then fell about 28 per cent to 69.32 tCO2e by 2024, mainly from forest-to-cropland conversion, and the massif stayed a net sink.
gap_quote: In the Congo Basin, however, LULCC-associated carbon dynamics remain poorly quantified at local scales, particularly in Cameroon.

place: Cameroon, humid forest zone of southern Cameroon
data: not stated
method: field study of a slash-and-burn land use chronosequence, carbon and nutrient stock and flow measurements, nutrient balance scenarios, on-farm planted fallow trials
finding: Forest felling and burning cut vegetation carbon from 199 to 102 Mg per ha in essep and 64 in banana fields, and Inga edulis fallows raised biomass and maize yields.
gap_quote: Yield declines in farmers' fields were attributed to diseases and weed infestation (56%) and soil properties (44%).

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Upper-Katanga, Miombo woodland, twenty community forest concessions
data: Landsat images
method: Landsat classification with NDVI in the colour composite, landscape indices of area, perimeter and number of patches
measures: accuracy and kappa above 90 per cent
finding: Community forestry raised forest area over 80 per cent in each concession from 2017 to 2019, but forest area fell after Covid-19, from 2019 to 2021.
gap_quote: Thus, community forestry serves as a management tool to address the numerous pressures on the Katangian open forest (Miombo Woodland), including deforestation and land cover changes which alter the structure and dynamics of vegetation cover and increase climate change effects.

data: 10 m MapBiomas land-cover data
method: vulnerability-based avoided deforestation methodology, Livelihood Vulnerability Index from a household survey, locality-matched dynamic baseline
finding: The dynamic baseline gave 0.70 per cent annual deforestation and 2,540 tCO2e baseline emissions, 2,032 creditable, worth about 40,000 to 80,000 US dollars a year.
gap_quote: Smallholders account for a growing share of forest loss while holding a disproportionate capacity to conserve and restore forests.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, protected area at the eastern border
data: SPOT high resolution images
method: automated object-based change detection with multidate segmentation and a multivariate iterative trimming test
finding: Automated object-based change detection on SPOT images mapped deforestation in an eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo protected area with 84 per cent overall accuracy.
gap_quote: Deforestation still nowadays occurs at an alarming rate in tropical regions.

place: pantropical, Latin America, Central Africa, Southeast Asia
data: more than 100 published field-based papers
method: systematic review of more than 100 field-based papers
finding: Land-use change in tropical peatlands more than doubled CO2 efflux while lowering CH4, and managed peat had higher bulk density, suggesting subsidence, with Central African peat averaging 250 cm thick.
gap_quote: The drainage, conversion, and degradation of natural tropical peatlands for agricultural development shifts the magnitude and direction of their carbon balance, from net carbon sinks to sources.

data: forest loss time series, product not named
method: similarity of environmental time series between spillover and non-spillover years, model of human factors and spillover occurrence
predictors: vegetation health, rainfall, temperature, forest loss, human population size
finding: No single environmental trigger preceded Ebola spillovers in Central Africa from 1990 to 2022, some following atypical conditions and others typical ones, and human factors showed no association.
gap_quote: Orthoebolavirus zairense (EBOV) is one example, circulating in wildlife in Central and West Africa, with high mortality in humans and animals.

data: land cover maps of 1990, 2000 and 2011 from the Ministry of Environment and Forestry, Indonesian topographic map
method: Land Change Modeler and Geomod
predictors: distance from forest edge, distance from roads, distance from streams, distance from settlement, elevation, slope
validation: later year held out, 2011 simulated from 1990 and 2000 maps and compared with the observed 2011 map, Land Change Modeler compared with Geomod
measures: Relative Operating Characteristic, value not stated
finding: Poso Regency lost 19,944 ha of forest from 1990 to 2011, 949 ha a year, and the Land Change Modeler suited deforestation assessment better than Geomod.
gap_quote: The forest destruction, climate change and global warming can reduce an indirect forest benefit because forest is the largest carbon sink and it plays a very important role in global carbon cycle.

place: Congo Basin, FSC-certified and artisanal logging sites
data: Sentinel-1 dense time series, 23,759 tree felling gap locations, multi-date drone lidar
method: Fused-Lasso Change Detection and Cumulative Sum change detection on Sentinel-1 time series
validation: independent reference sample of 23,759 felling gaps and drone lidar, fused-lasso compared with CuSum
measures: confirmed gap rates, value not stated, mean felling date difference minus 2 days for fused-lasso and minus 19 days for CuSum in FSC-certified areas
finding: Fused-lasso and CuSum Sentinel-1 methods confirmed similar shares of felling gaps, rising with gap size, and fused-lasso dated felling more closely in FSC-certified areas, 2 days against 19.
gap_quote: Deforestation and forest degradation are the main threats to biodiversity and carbon stocks in tropical forests.

place: Indonesia, Central Sulawesi, Morowali Utara District
data: land use or cover maps of 2003, 2009 and 2015
method: logistic regression, REDD+ model of business as usual deforestation and carbon emissions
predictors: distance from forest edge, distance from roads, distance from streams, slope
finding: Morowali Utara lost 62,017.47 ha of forest from 2003 to 2015, 5,168.12 ha a year, and a REDD project could protect up to 18.868 million tCO2e.
gap_quote: Land use cover conversion from forest to another land was constributing for total green houses gas (GHS) emission, especially from forestry sector.

place: Congo Basin, central Congo Basin peatlands
data: drainage land-use scenario, data not named
method: peatland carbon model driven by an ensemble of 10 climate models, with and without drainage
finding: Supplementary material to a study finding that drainage with climate change would make Congo Basin peatlands significant carbon emitters, peat thinning 2.6 m at 3 °C.
gap_quote: By contrast, simulations that couple land-use change with twenty-first-century climate change are unequivocal: the Congo Basin peatlands will become significant emitters of carbon.

place: Congo Basin, Tridom Dja-Odzala-Minkébé transboundary conservation landscape
data: survey of 1035 rural households, deforestation data not stated
method: spatial autoregressive probit model, spatial lag model, limited dependent variable models
predictors: livelihood strategies, neighbouring household deforestation, with strategies explained by financial assets, distance to market, human-elephant conflict damage and indigeneity
finding: Household deforestation intensity varied with livelihood strategy, and imitation among neighbouring households created spatial spillovers that could amplify small-scale deforestation in the Tridom landscape.
gap_quote: En effet, nous trouvons qu’il existe des effets d’imitation, dans la décision de déforestation, entre les ménages d’un même voisinage, avec des effets spatiaux indirects susceptibles d’amplifier la déforestation à petite échelle.

period: 2000 to 2020 forest loss, 2014 to 2022 threat status
data: tree cover loss quantified in Google Earth Engine, product not named
method: richness-risk index, GIS analysis of primate ranges, forest loss within ranges in Google Earth Engine
predictors: species richness, extinction risk, forest loss within ranges
finding: Threatened primate species rose 20 per cent from 2014 to 2022 and ranges lost 10 to 30 per cent of forest, with the Congo River Basin a richness-risk hotspot.
gap_quote: Areas of especially high species richness and extinction risk include the Amazon and Congo River Basins, equatorial West Africa, Borneo, and eastern Madagascar.

place: pantropical, Amazon Basin, Borneo, Congo Basin
data: remote sensing products distinguishing degraded and secondary forest and carbon sequestration, not named
method: space-for-time substitution with remote sensing products
finding: Recovering degraded forests, 10 per cent of forest area, had a large carbon sink potential, secondary forests grew faster, and 35 per cent of degraded forest was later deforested.
gap_quote: However, the size of this sink is declining due to human activities such as deforestation and forest degradation through logging and fire, as well as climate variability and change

data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: VCS REDD+ outcomes were mixed, some projects cutting forest loss and others overstating carbon benefits through baselines, permanence and leakage, so stronger ex-post causal validation was needed.
gap_quote: Overall, evidence from quasi-experimental and global syntheses (2015–2025) shows heterogeneous outcomes: some VCS-backed activities yield real reductions in forest loss, while others overstate carbon benefits due to baseline construction, permanence and leakage challenges.

data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Deforestation in the Congo Basin was low, 0.09 to 0.17 per cent a year, driven by slash-and-burn and commercial farming and infrastructure, but emergence plans could bring massive forest loss.
gap_quote: All the Basin countries are hoping for emergence, but their timelines are different: 2035 for DRC and Cameroon, 2025 for Gabon and 2020 for Equatorial Guinea. Their emergence programmes are largely dependent on the development of infrastructure and industry and may entail massive destruction of forestlands.

data: forest fragmentation classes, airborne canopy height and above ground biomass estimates, forest cover product not named
method: fragmentation analysis of forest edges, analysis of variance of canopy height and biomass by edge width, change analysis
finding: Degradation caused at least a quarter of biomass loss, intact primary forest fell 3.5 per cent over 15 years, and degradation affected up to three times the deforested area.
gap_quote: Recent studies have shown that fragmentation is an increasing threat to global forests, which has major impacts on biodiversity and the important ecosystem services provided by forested landscapes.

data: not stated
method: G4M global forest model linked with the GLOBIOM global land-use model
predictors: carbon price, land and forest product prices
validation: compared with independent projections for Ukraine
finding: A 25 dollar per tC carbon price would sequester an extra 15 Gt C over 50 years, led by Brazil, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Indonesia.
gap_quote: Carbon sequestration and avoided CO2 emissions from deforestation are hotly debated issues in the negotiations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

data: NOAA AVHRR Local Area Coverage at 1 km and Global Area Coverage at 8 km, ancillary data
method: land cover classification fusing AVHRR LAC and GAC data with ancillary information
validation: field visits and Landsat MSS imagery
measures: forest cover type mapping errors at most 20 per cent
finding: A 1 km AVHRR land cover map of central Africa showed dense humid forest, degraded forest and savanna classes, with forest type errors of at most 20 per cent.
gap_quote: Forest cover type mapping errors were at most 20 per cent.

place: Cameroon, North Region, Bouba-Ndjida and Bénoué National Parks, Mayo-Rey department
data: Sentinel-2 imagery of 2016, 2020 and 2025
method: GIS classification of Sentinel-2 imagery, transition matrices and rates of change, analysis of the legislative and institutional framework
validation: kappa assessment, reference data not stated
finding: Bénoué lost woody vegetation faster than Bouba-Ndjida, deforestation 5.44 against 1.87 per cent a year, which the study linked to fragmented, under-resourced and overlapping governance.
gap_quote: The conservation of biodiversity in Cameroon – a country often referred to as ‘Africa in miniature’ due to its great ecological diversity – is coming up against increasing ecosystem degradation.

data: WorldView-2 imagery at 0.5 and 2 m, SRTM 90 m terrain model, field survey of over 450 points
method: object-based hierarchical classification with segmentation
measures: roads and buildings 95 per cent, burnt areas 86 per cent, food crops 96 per cent, annual crops 90 per cent, agroforests 92 per cent, modern cocoa plantation 92 per cent, palm groves 98 per cent
finding: Object-based classification of 2011 WorldView-2 imagery separated cocoa agroforests, plantations and palm groves in Cameroon with class accuracies of 86 to 98 per cent.
gap_quote: WORLDVIEW2 acquisition at 0.5/2m in 8 bands (Feb.2011,very cloudy…)

data: JRC Tropical Moist Forest annual change, GLAD dataset, ESA land cover, photo-interpreted agricultural landscapes
method: multi-source assembly with explicit prioritization among datasets and reclassification rules
finding: A land cover and land use map of the Republic of the Congo was released, merging TMF, GLAD, ESA and photo-interpreted data, with cropland split by clearing origin.
gap_quote: the available land-use and land-cover (LULC) datasets, when considered individually, proved insufficient or exhibited limited accuracy, particularly for the characterization of agricultural development areas.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Bukavu, Cyangugu, Goma and Gisenyi
data: Landsat and SPOT images
method: object-based and pixel-based classification, morphological neighbourhood classification, sampled population survey
predictors: urban growth, land use, built-up density, neighbourhood structure, population density
finding: The study set out to map 30 years of urban growth in Bukavu and Goma from Landsat and SPOT, comparing object-based and pixel-based classification, and estimate population and geo-hazard vulnerability.
gap_quote: In Central Africa, population data are not easily collected, and when available, not always reliable.

data: remote sensing tree cover data and global databases, product not named
method: random forest model, simulations under climate and land-use scenarios
predictors: annual rainfall, accumulated water deficit, edaphic factors, fire, agricultural practices, pastoralism, population
finding: Rainfall and water deficit mainly set tree cover in Central Africa, but agriculture, especially pastoralism, mattered, and simulated land-use change could offset climate effects.
gap_quote: But its determinants and their relative importance are still a matter of debate, especially because most regional and global analyses have not considered the influence of agricultural practices.

data: district deforestation panel data, source not stated
method: spatial econometric panel models, spatial autoregressive model selected
predictors: spatial lag of neighbouring district deforestation, other predictors not named
validation: compared with rival spatial model forms
finding: A spatial autoregressive model best fitted district deforestation in Indonesia, showing strong inter-district dependence, so deforestation spread between neighbours and conservation could spill over positively.
gap_quote: A key element in the implementation of an effective result-based mechanism for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation (REDD+) is the reference level (RL).

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kasai Basin, 24 hillslope transects along the Kasai River
data: not stated
method: sampling of over 6000 soils on 24 hillslope transects, carbon, nitrogen and stable isotopes, texture, clay mineralogy, fallout radionuclides, MIR spectroscopy
finding: Preliminary results showed soil organic carbon of 0.30 to 2.5 per cent in the upper 40 cm, varying with depth, slope position, climate and land use.
gap_quote: The Kasai Basin, located in the southwestern part of the Congo River Basin, displays a unique array of climatic conditions, mineralogical compositions and land use trajectories. It is currently experiencing an explosive demographic expansion, which leads to drastic deforestation for cropland expansion.

place: Gabon, estuary mangroves, northern and southern sites
data: not stated
method: soil organic carbon sampling to 1 m depth under Rhizophora racemosa and Avicennia germinans, comparison of northern and southern sites
finding: Mean mangrove soil organic carbon to 1 m was 256.28 plus or minus 127.29 MgC per ha, higher in Rhizophora racemosa than Avicennia germinans, and about twice upland forest soils.
gap_quote: To address this gap, determining the SOC spatial variation in Gabonese’s estuarine is essential for better understanding the global carbon cycle.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kundelungu National Park
data: Landsat images of 2001, 2008, 2015 and 2022
method: Landsat classification, landscape metrics, decision tree of spatial transformation processes, fire risk assessment from annual burnt areas
finding: Forest in Kundelungu National Park fell from 2339 to 1596 km2 between 2001 and 2022, deforestation 0.8 to 3.4 per cent a year, as illegal farming and fires doubled disturbance.
gap_quote: In the Kundelungu National Park (KNP), southeast of the Democratic Republic of Congo, illicit human activities including recurrent bushfires contribute to constant regression of forest cover.

area: 65 000 km2, with a 7500 km2 protected area
data: satellite-based forest cover, sensor not named
method: satellite-based spatially explicit deforestation model, two RED implementation scenarios
predictors: oil palm plantation expansion, road construction, protected area, accessibility
finding: RED limited to the upland protected area would save 1313 km2 by 2030 while outside forest shrank 22 per cent, against 7824 km2 saved if applied across all unprotected forest.
gap_quote: Meanwhile, new roads are currently under construction, while companies are converting lowland forests into oil palm plantations.

data: land cover, source not stated
method: analytical hierarchy process in GIS
predictors: elevation, drainage density, distance to the river, land cover
validation: flood points collected in the field after a flood
finding: Elevation, drainage density, distance to the river and land cover mainly drove flooding in the Tongo Bassa basin, and the high risk class matched field flood points.
gap_quote: Like most of the world's major cities, Douala is subject to floods.

data: Hansen global deforestation dataset, Worldpop, NDVI, field observations
method: erosion modelling of 101 watersheds, model not named, analysis of spatial drivers
predictors: rainfall erosivity, elevation variation, topographical roughness, NDVI, population density, Hansen deforestation
finding: Rainfall erosivity, elevation variation, topographical roughness, NDVI and population density significantly drove erosion across 101 Congo Basin watersheds, and human activities were accelerating erosion.
gap_quote: A prime example of these issues and consequences is the Congo Basin (CB), which contains the second-largest tropical forest in the world and is currently experiencing an explosive demographic expansion, leading to drastic land use and land cover changes (LULCC), such as deforestation and cropland expansion.
